symbols.name: wire count
symbols.meaning: The number of wires of the network, $W_{\rm b}$ or $W_{\rm c}$ for the two constructions.
symbols.quote: Subspace labels from three-element subsets are nested nondegenerate subspaces that keep a network's total edge rank below $Wm$, where $W$ counts wires and $m$ is the label dimension.

symbols.name: label dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the label space, which is $h^3$.
symbols.quote: Subspace labels from three-element subsets are nested nondegenerate subspaces that keep a network's total edge rank below $Wm$, where $W$ counts wires and $m$ is the label dimension.

symbols.name: label
symbols.meaning: A label, the smaller member of a nested pair $U\subset V$.
symbols.quote: Each label $U$ has projection $P_U,$ and for nested labels $U\subset V,$ $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on the residual $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its complement, so an edge costs rank $\dim V-\dim U.$

symbols.name: larger label
symbols.meaning: A label, the larger member of a nested pair $U\subset V$.
symbols.quote: Each label $U$ has projection $P_U,$ and for nested labels $U\subset V,$ $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on the residual $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its complement, so an edge costs rank $\dim V-\dim U.$

symbols.name: label projection
symbols.meaning: The projection onto a label $U$ along $U^\perp$.
symbols.quote: Each label $U$ has projection $P_U,$ and for nested labels $U\subset V,$ $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on the residual $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its complement, so an edge costs rank $\dim V-\dim U.$

symbols.name: vertex
symbols.meaning: A vertex of the network.
symbols.quote: They are used as frames in [Frames on wire arrays](common-frame-principle.md): vertex $v$ carries $M_v=P_{U_v}.$

symbols.name: vertex frame matrix
symbols.meaning: The frame matrix at vertex $v$, the projection of its label.
symbols.quote: They are used as frames in [Frames on wire arrays](common-frame-principle.md): vertex $v$ carries $M_v=P_{U_v}.$

symbols.name: vertex label
symbols.meaning: The label of vertex $v$.
symbols.quote: They are used as frames in [Frames on wire arrays](common-frame-principle.md): vertex $v$ carries $M_v=P_{U_v}.$

symbols.name: bilinear space
symbols.meaning: The bilinear space $\mathbb Q^h$ of the bit network or $\mathbb F_2^h$ of the complex network.
symbols.quote: For the bit network $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle p,g\rangle=p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)g,$ $J$ the all-ones matrix; for the complex network $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product.

symbols.name: all-ones matrix
symbols.meaning: The matrix with every entry equal to one.
symbols.quote: For the bit network $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle p,g\rangle=p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)g,$ $J$ the all-ones matrix; for the complex network $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product.

symbols.name: bilinear form argument
symbols.meaning: A vector of $F$ in the bilinear form of the bit network.
symbols.quote: For the bit network $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle p,g\rangle=p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)g,$ $J$ the all-ones matrix; for the complex network $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product.

symbols.name: bilinear form argument
symbols.meaning: A vector of $F$ in the bilinear form of the bit network.
symbols.quote: For the bit network $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle p,g\rangle=p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)g,$ $J$ the all-ones matrix; for the complex network $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product.

symbols.name: ground-set size
symbols.meaning: The number of points in the ground set, here 100.
symbols.quote: Triples $S,T$ in a ground set of $h=100$ points have indicators $t_S,t_T.$

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A triple, a 3-element subset of the ground set.
symbols.quote: Triples $S,T$ in a ground set of $h=100$ points have indicators $t_S,t_T.$

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A triple, a 3-element subset of the ground set.
symbols.quote: Triples $S,T$ in a ground set of $h=100$ points have indicators $t_S,t_T.$

symbols.name: triple indicator
symbols.meaning: The indicator vector of the triple $S$.
symbols.quote: Triples $S,T$ in a ground set of $h=100$ points have indicators $t_S,t_T.$

symbols.name: triple indicator
symbols.meaning: The indicator vector of the triple $T$.
symbols.quote: Triples $S,T$ in a ground set of $h=100$ points have indicators $t_S,t_T.$

symbols.name: label space
symbols.meaning: The label space $F^{\otimes3}$.
symbols.quote: The label space $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ has dimension $m=h^3.$

symbols.name: input
symbols.meaning: An input, named by a triple of triple indices $(a_1,a_2,a_3)$.
symbols.quote: An input $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of three triples has label $U_a=\langle u_a\rangle,$ where $u_a=t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}.$

symbols.name: input tensor
symbols.meaning: The pure tensor $t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$ of input $a$.
symbols.quote: An input $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of three triples has label $U_a=\langle u_a\rangle,$ where $u_a=t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}.$

symbols.name: input label
symbols.meaning: The label of input $a$, the line spanned by $u_a$.
symbols.quote: An input $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of three triples has label $U_a=\langle u_a\rangle,$ where $u_a=t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}.$

symbols.name: input role
symbols.meaning: The input role of $a$, whose source is the label $U_a$.
symbols.quote: $X_a$ has source $U_a$ and sink $\mathcal F,$ $Y_a$ has source $0$ and sink $U_a^\perp,$ and scratch roles have source $0$ and sink $\mathcal F.$

symbols.name: paired role
symbols.meaning: The role paired with $X_a$, whose sink is $U_a^\perp$.
symbols.quote: $X_a$ has source $U_a$ and sink $\mathcal F,$ $Y_a$ has source $0$ and sink $U_a^\perp,$ and scratch roles have source $0$ and sink $\mathcal F.$

symbols.name: input count
symbols.meaning: The number of inputs $a$, each contributing one source dimension.
symbols.quote: Each $U_a$ is a line, so sources total $N,$ one per input, and sinks $Wm-N.$

symbols.name: stage index
symbols.meaning: The index of the current stage, which exposes the $j$th tensor factor.
symbols.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

symbols.name: stage space
symbols.meaning: The tensor space $F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ at stage $j$.
symbols.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

symbols.name: stage line
symbols.meaning: The line spanned by the first $j-1$ triple tensors.
symbols.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

symbols.name: stage complement
symbols.meaning: The complement $R^\perp$ of $R$ inside $A$.
symbols.quote: At stage $j$ let $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)},$ $R=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=R^\perp$ in $A.$

symbols.name: invocation count
symbols.meaning: The number of invocations of the repeated block.
symbols.quote: With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$

symbols.name: central wires
symbols.meaning: The number of central wires in one invocation.
symbols.quote: With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$

symbols.name: total loss
symbols.meaning: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges.
symbols.quote: With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$

symbols.name: orthogonal sum
symbols.meaning: The orthogonal direct sum of two subspaces.
symbols.quote: Gate labels at times $0$ to $7$ are $B\otimes\langle t_T\rangle,$ $B\otimes F,$ $(B\otimes F)\oplus(R\otimes\langle t_T\rangle),$ $A\otimes F,$ $B\otimes F,$ $(B\otimes F)\oplus(R\otimes\langle t_T\rangle^\perp),$ $A\otimes F,$ $A\otimes F,$ with $\oplus$ the orthogonal sum.

symbols.name: total edge rank
symbols.meaning: The total rank of all edge changes.
symbols.quote: Bit network: $-P_{U_a}$ replaces $M_v$ at the source of $X_a;$ then $P_{U_a^\perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m$ makes every endpoint difference $I_m.$ Edge ranks equal dimension changes, except at the $N$ source edges, where $2P_{U_a}$ has rank one. Write $s$ for the total edge rank, so $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m.$

symbols.name: two-point kernel
symbols.meaning: The matrix $H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H$.
symbols.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

symbols.name: Hadamard matrix
symbols.meaning: The normalized Hadamard matrix.
symbols.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

symbols.name: kernel coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient $\frac{1+i}{2}$ of the identity in $C$.
symbols.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

symbols.name: kernel coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient $\frac{1-i}{2}$ of $\sigma$ in $C$.
symbols.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

symbols.name: coordinate swap
symbols.meaning: The matrix that interchanges the two coordinates.
symbols.quote: Complex network: $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\alpha I+\beta\sigma,$ with $H$ the Hadamard matrix, $\alpha=\frac{1+i}{2},$ $\beta=\frac{1-i}{2}$ and $\sigma$ the coordinate swap.

symbols.name: phase frame
symbols.meaning: The phase frame of label $U$ on functions of binary vectors.
symbols.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

symbols.name: phase exponent
symbols.meaning: The phase exponent $|P_Ux|\bmod 4$ of label $U$.
symbols.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

symbols.name: binary vector
symbols.meaning: A binary vector in $\mathbb F_2^m$.
symbols.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

symbols.name: Hamming weight
symbols.meaning: The number of ones in a binary vector.
symbols.quote: Frames over binary $x$ are $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m},$ with $q_U(x)=|P_Ux|\bmod4$ and $|\cdot|$ the Hamming weight.

symbols.name: orthonormal basis
symbols.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the residual $E$.
symbols.quote: For an orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$ of a residual $E,$ $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal K}|w|\,(w\cdot x\bmod2)\pmod4,$ with $|w|$ odd.

symbols.name: residual
symbols.meaning: The orthogonal residual of an edge.
symbols.quote: For an orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$ of a residual $E,$ $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal K}|w|\,(w\cdot x\bmod2)\pmod4,$ with $|w|$ odd.

symbols.name: basis vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of the orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$.
symbols.quote: For an orthonormal basis $\mathcal K$ of a residual $E,$ $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal K}|w|\,(w\cdot x\bmod2)\pmod4,$ with $|w|$ odd.

symbols.name: translation
symbols.meaning: The translation by a binary vector $w$.
symbols.quote: Each factor $i^{\pm(w\cdot x\bmod2)}$ is a kernel $\alpha I+\beta\tau_w$ or its inverse, since $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=\sigma$ turns $(-1)^{w\cdot x}$ into a translation $\tau_w.$

symbols.name: sign matrix
symbols.meaning: The diagonal sign matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$.
symbols.quote: The pair $X_a\to Y_a$ has inverse kernels, which $C=iZC^{-1}Z$ with $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ turns into $C,$ so every role carries $C^{\otimes m}.$

relations.quote: The labels are attached to the gates and terminals of a [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](linear-network.md).
They are used as frames in [Frames on wire arrays](common-frame-principle.md): vertex $v$ carries $M_v=P_{U_v}.$
The labels are based on [Rank, subspaces and orthogonal complements](linear-algebra-basics.md).

derivations.quote: Since $t_S,t_T$ have three ones, $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2,$ so each triple line is nondegenerate.

$X_a$ has source $U_a$ and sink $\mathcal F,$ $Y_a$ has source $0$ and sink $U_a^\perp,$ and scratch roles have source $0$ and sink $\mathcal F.$ Each $U_a$ is a line, so sources total $N,$ one per input, and sinks $Wm-N.$
The next stage has $A'=A\otimes F,$ $R'=R\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$ and $B'=(R')^\perp,$ so outgoing labels equal the next incoming ones.
Dimension drops only on central edges from time $3$ to $4,$ each by $h.$ With $\nu$ invocations of $c$ central wires each, total loss $L=\nu ch.$
and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539,$ both below one half, so $N$ extra source ranks leave a strict saving.

Bit network: $-P_{U_a}$ replaces $M_v$ at the source of $X_a;$ then $P_{U_a^\perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m$ makes every endpoint difference $I_m.$ Edge ranks equal dimension changes, except at the $N$ source edges, where $2P_{U_a}$ has rank one. Write $s$ for the total edge rank, so $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m.$

Each factor $i^{\pm(w\cdot x\bmod2)}$ is a kernel $\alpha I+\beta\tau_w$ or its inverse, since $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=\sigma$ turns $(-1)^{w\cdot x}$ into a translation $\tau_w.$ Over $\mathbb F_2$ residuals have orthonormal bases, so $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m.$
